column1: table|What makes a meal feel welcoming to you?|meal,sharing,serving,portion|Do you prefer a big dinner or something simple?~Something simple, if it leaves time to talk.~Would soup and bread suit you?~Perfect. I can bring the bread.~Then I will make the soup.~And we can share the washing-up afterward.|Your guest says they prefer simple food. Suggest a meal and ask one relevant follow-up.|How about soup and bread? Is there anything you would prefer not to eat?

journey|How do you choose where to go for a short trip?|train,station,itinerary,map|Do you plan every stop before a trip?~Only the travel. I like leaving part of the day open.~What happens if the weather changes?~I keep one indoor option in mind.~Have you ever found somewhere better by changing the plan?~A little gallery became the best part of our last trip.|A friend likes leaving an afternoon unplanned. Ask a follow-up that invites an experience rather than a yes/no answer.|What is the best place you have discovered by changing your plan?

home|What makes a room comfortable for you?|room,chair,window,clothes,minimal|Have you changed anything in your room recently?~I moved the chair closer to the window.~Has it made much difference?~I read there more often now.~Did you need to buy anything?~No. Moving what I already had was enough.|A friend says moving a chair made the room better. Ask a relevant follow-up without turning it into a shopping recommendation.|What is it about the new position that makes it more comfortable?

books|What have you enjoyed reading lately?|book,reading,library,dictionary|Have you read anything you would recommend?~A short book of travel stories.~What did you enjoy about it?~The writer notices small details rather than rushing between landmarks.~Would you lend it to me when you finish?~Certainly. I have one chapter left.|Your friend recommends a book. Ask about what they enjoyed rather than testing whether they remember the plot.|What stayed with you after you finished reading it?

conversation|What helps you feel heard in a conversation?|listening,discussion,tea,sharing|Do you prefer someone to offer advice straight away?~Usually I need them to listen first.~Would you tell them that directly?~I might say that I need to talk it through before deciding.~That would help me respond better.~And I can ask for suggestions when I am ready.|A friend says they need to be heard before receiving advice. Respond without immediately offering a solution.|Of course. I am listening. Would you like to tell me what happened?

market|How do you decide what is worth buying?|shopping,market,produce,budget,saving|Do you make a list before shopping?~A short one. Otherwise I buy things I already have.~Do you stick to it exactly?~Not if I find something useful at a good price.~How do you decide whether it is useful?~I ask where I would use it, rather than just noticing the discount.|Someone says they bought an item because it was discounted. Ask a friendly question about its actual use.|What are you planning to use it for?

music|Is there an album you like listening to all the way through?|guitar,music,headphones,music-work|Do you usually listen to whole albums?~Not often, but I tried it last weekend.~Did anything surprise you?~The quieter songs made more sense between the louder ones.~Would you listen that way again?~Yes, when I can give it my attention.|Invite someone to explain how listening to an album in order changed their experience.|Did the order of the tracks change how you heard any of the songs?

weather|What do you enjoy doing on a rainy day?|rain,storm,tea,book,room|Has the rain spoiled your plans?~It changed them. I am going to visit the library instead.~Would you like some company?~Yes. We could stop for tea afterward.~Shall we check when it closes?~Good idea. I would rather not arrive just as they lock up.|A friend has replaced a walk with a library visit. Continue the conversation with one practical question.|What time does the library close?

work|What makes working together easier for you?|community,strategy,whiteboard,helping|What helped the group finish on time?~Knowing who was responsible for each task.~Did you have to supervise everyone?~No. We agreed when to check in and let people get on with it.~Would you change anything next time?~Leave more time for the final cleanup.|Your colleague mentions a smooth handover. Ask what specifically made it work.|What information did the next person need when you handed the task over?

city|What do you notice when you explore a new neighborhood?|city,walk,crossing,market|Do you head straight for the main sights?~I usually walk a little first.~What catches your eye?~Small shops and places where people stop to talk.~Would you rather explore alone or with a local?~Both give you a different view. A local can explain things I might miss.|A visitor enjoys small neighborhood details. Suggest an outing and explain why it may appeal.|We could walk through the market street; you can see the small shops and how people use the space.

garden|How did you first become interested in growing things?|plant,watering,leaf,growth,community|Was your first plant easy to look after?~Not really. I watered it too often.~What helped you improve?~Checking the soil rather than following the same rule every day.~Would you recommend starting with one plant?~Yes. It gives you time to notice what it needs.|A friend says they often overwater plants. Ask about their observations rather than diagnosing the cause.|What do you usually notice about the soil before you water it?

year|What would you like to keep doing next year?|notebook,calendar,walk,relaxing|Is there a change you are pleased you made?~I started taking a short walk after lunch.~Will you set a bigger target next year?~I might just keep the habit as it is.~Because it already does what you need?~Exactly. Not everything has to become more ambitious.|Someone likes a modest habit and does not want a larger target. Acknowledge that choice without pushing improvement.|That makes sense. What do you enjoy about keeping it just as it is?

newyear|Is there one small thing you would like to try this year?|calendar,notebook,morning,walk|Are you making a big list of goals?~No. I would like to read a little after breakfast.~What would make that easy to begin?~Leaving a book beside the kettle.~Would you like to compare what we read next month?~Yes. That sounds more inviting than counting pages.|Suggest a small shared New Year activity without making it a competition.|We could read for ten minutes a few mornings a week and talk about anything we enjoyed.

valentine|How do you like to show someone you appreciate them?|valentine,wrapping,sharing,tea|Do you usually buy a Valentine's gift?~Sometimes, but I often write a note to a friend.~What do you put in it?~One specific thing I am grateful for.~That sounds less pressured than a grand gesture.~It feels more like what I actually want to say.|A friend prefers a personal note to an expensive gift. Ask about a specific kind act they might mention.|Is there something they did recently that you would like to thank them for?

lunarnewyear|Is there a New Year custom that matters to your family?|lunar,lunar-lantern,family,sharing|Will you be celebrating Lunar New Year with your family?~Yes. We are meeting for a meal.~Is there anything visitors should know?~It is best to ask the host; families do things differently.~I would enjoy hearing about your own custom, if you would like to share it.~My grandmother usually explains the dishes and the stories behind them.|You are invited to an unfamiliar celebration. Ask a respectful practical question without assuming every family follows the same custom.|Is there anything your family would like visitors to know before the meal?

easter|Are you doing anything for Easter this year?|easter-hunt,easter,basket,sharing|Are you organizing the egg hunt?~Yes, but there will be another activity for anyone who prefers it.~What will that be?~Decorating cards at the table.~Can I help explain the boundary for the hunt?~That would be useful. We want the instructions to be clear.|A guest prefers not to join the egg hunt. Offer another activity without asking them to justify the choice.|You are welcome to decorate a card at the table instead.

earthday|Is there an everyday change you have found easy to keep?|recycling,bag,watering,community|Did the refill bottle make a difference to your routine?~Yes, once I started leaving it by my keys.~So remembering it was the hard part?~Exactly. Buying it did not automatically change the habit.~Would that idea work for a reusable bag too?~It might. Put it where you already pause before leaving.|Ask about what makes a reusable item part of an actual habit rather than just a purchase.|What helps you remember to take it with you?

mothersday|Is there someone you would like to thank this weekend?|family,valentine,sharing,serving|Are you planning something for Mother's Day?~I am making lunch for the person who usually does the cooking.~Have you asked what she would enjoy?~Yes. She asked for a quiet afternoon rather than a big gathering.~That sounds easy to respect.~And it gives us a clearer plan than guessing.|Someone asks for a quiet afternoon rather than a party. Respond in a way that respects the request.|Of course. We can keep lunch simple and leave the afternoon free.

fathersday|What do you enjoy doing with someone who has cared for you?|family,walk,sharing,guitar|Have you chosen a Father's Day activity?~We are going for a short walk.~Does he enjoy long routes?~No, so we will stay near home and stop for tea.~A familiar route can leave more space to talk.~That is what we are looking forward to.|Suggest a shared activity for someone who enjoys conversation but prefers not to walk far.|We could take a short walk nearby and stop for tea.

independenceday|Are you going to the neighborhood celebration?|independence,city,sharing,community|Will you watch the parade?~For a little while. I prefer a quieter place afterward.~Do you have a meeting point?~Yes, beside the library entrance.~I will let you know if I join you.~Please do. It can be hard to find people once it gets busy.|A friend may join you at a crowded parade. Give a clear meeting arrangement without promising instant contact by phone.|Meet us beside the library entrance at eleven; if the plan changes, I will tell you before we leave.

halloween|What would you like to do for Halloween?|pumpkin,halloween-candy,ornament,sharing|What would you like to do for Halloween, if anything?~Something low-key. I am not really into haunted houses.~How about carving a pumpkin and making dinner?~That sounds more like me. Have you tried an elaborate design?~Once. It collapsed before we finished eating.~Then let us choose a face we can actually finish.|Your neighbor says they do not celebrate Halloween. Acknowledge that and smoothly open another topic.|Of course. Are you doing anything nice this weekend instead?

thanksgiving|Is there a dish or memory you like sharing at Thanksgiving?|meal,portion,serving,sharing|What are you bringing to the meal?~A dish my uncle used to make.~Will you tell everyone the story behind it?~If they are interested. I do not want to turn dinner into a speech.~A short story might invite others to share theirs.~Then I will leave room for that too.|A guest mentions a family dish. Ask an inviting question without demanding a long personal story.|Is there a memory you associate with that dish, if you feel like sharing it?

christmas|What would make this Christmas feel relaxed for you?|christmas,wrapping,ornament,tea|Are you looking forward to the gathering?~Yes, though I would like to keep the preparations simple.~What could we leave out?~A large gift exchange. We could bring one shared dish instead.~Let us check that everyone is comfortable with that.~Then nobody has to guess what is expected.|Suggest a lower-pressure alternative to a large gift exchange and invite agreement.|Would everyone be comfortable bringing one shared dish instead of exchanging gifts?

tea|Would you like some tea?|tea,water,serving|Would you like some tea?~Yes, please. A small cup would be lovely.~Do you take milk?~No, thank you. Just tea.~Shall we sit by the window?~That sounds good.|Your guest declines milk. Continue the conversation without offering it again.|Of course. Would you like to sit by the window?

sunday|Do you have any plans for Sunday?|calendar,map,sharing|Do you have any plans for Sunday?~Nothing fixed. I thought I might visit the market.~Would you like some company?~Yes, if you are free in the morning.~Shall we meet at the entrance at ten?~That works for me.|Turn a tentative market visit into a clear arrangement with a place and time.|Shall we meet at the market entrance at ten on Sunday morning?

rewarding|What has been the most rewarding part so far?|community,growth,plant|What has been the most rewarding part of the garden project?~Seeing people return and help one another.~Not just watching the plants grow?~That matters too, but the connections were the surprise.~Was there a moment when you noticed that change?~When a new volunteer came back simply to check on someone else.|Ask a follow-up about a specific moment that made a project feel rewarding.|Was there a particular moment when you felt the work had made a difference?

teamwork|Has this changed how you approach teamwork?|strategy,whiteboard,community|Has the workshop changed how you work with other people?~I now explain what a handover needs to include.~Did that solve every difficulty?~No, but fewer tasks fall between roles.~What would you try next?~Making space for people to say when an arrangement is not working.|Invite a concrete example of improved teamwork without assuming all difficulties have disappeared.|Can you give an example of a handover that works better now?

unexamined|What assumption did the discussion leave unexamined?|document,discussion,strategy|What assumption did the discussion leave unexamined?~That everyone could book online.~Was that ever stated as a condition?~No. It shaped the proposal without becoming visible.~How could the next discussion test it?~By asking who would be excluded and what an alternative would require.|Identify an assumption in a phone-only booking proposal and suggest a question that tests it.|Ask whether everyone can use a suitable phone and how someone without one could book.

morning-q|How is your morning going?|morning,tea,book|How is your morning going?~Well, thank you. I had time to read.~What did you read?~A short story.~Would you recommend it?~Yes. The ending made me smile.|Respond to I had time to read with a related question.|What did you read?

beforework|What do you like doing before work?|morning,tea,walk|What do you like doing before work?~I like a short walk.~Do you always have time?~Not every day, but I enjoy it when I can.~Is there a place nearby you like?~The little park at the end of the street.|A friend enjoys a short walk before work. Ask about where they go.|Is there a nearby route you particularly like?

newactivity|Have you tried anything new lately?|guitar,plant,repair|Have you tried anything new lately?~I have started learning a few guitar chords.~Was it difficult to begin?~My fingers were slow, but I could play a simple pattern.~What made you keep going?~Hearing a little improvement after a week.|Encourage a beginner without describing the activity as easy.|It sounds satisfying to notice the improvement. What would you like to learn next?

pace|What has been a welcome change of pace for you?|walk,watering,relaxing|What has been a welcome change of pace lately?~Helping in the garden after a week of desk work.~Was it the activity or the company that mattered?~A bit of both. I stopped watching the clock.~Would you make it a regular commitment?~Perhaps, but I would like to keep some of that openness.|A friend enjoys an activity because it feels open-ended. Ask about repeating it without imposing a target.|Would you enjoy doing it again when you have the chance?

choice|Which part of your routine feels most like a choice?|calendar,notebook,walk|Which part of your routine feels most like a choice?~The walk I take before going home.~What makes it different from the rest of the day?~I do not measure it or use it to finish another task.~Would fixing a target improve it?~For me, that might remove what I value about it.|Someone values an unmeasured walk. Respond without turning it into another goal.|It sounds as though the freedom is part of what makes it worthwhile.

unmeasured|What would you keep even if it offered no measurable benefit?|relaxing,sharing,music|What would you keep even if it offered no measurable benefit?~The unplanned conversations after our meetings.~Would you say they serve no purpose?~Not quite. I would resist reducing their value to a target.~Then the problem may be the measure rather than the conversation.~Or the assumption that value must always justify itself in measurable terms.|Distinguish something having no measured benefit from having no value.|A measure may fail to capture an experience's relational, emotional or intrinsic value.
